label: lem:bring-cone-reeb-quaternionic-twist
title: Reeb quaternionic twist on the Bring-cone link: $[M_i, M_j] = 2M_k$ and cyclic
html:
Lemma. Reeb quaternionic twist on the Bring-cone link: [M_i, M_j] = 2M_k and cyclic

The affine cone C(\mathcal{B}) of the tetraplectic structure is a real 4-manifold, so the link of its singularity is 3-dimensional. Where the bulk carries the invariant volume form, that link carries a 3-Sasakian (degenerate quaternionic-contact) structure: in place of a single Reeb vector field there is an \mathrm{SU}(2) triad of contact forms and dual Reeb fields.

Following Foth–Leitner [fothleitner2003] for quaternionic flag manifolds, model the triad on the quaternions by right-multiplication by the imaginary units — M_x(p) = p\,x for x \in \{\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf{k}\}, or in 2 \times 2 block form

  M_x = \begin{pmatrix} x & 0 \\ 0 & x \end{pmatrix} .

Write [M_x, M_y] := M_y \circ M_x - M_x \circ M_y. Then

  [M_x, M_y] \;=\; 2\,M_{x \cdot y}
  \qquad (x \neq y),

that is, [M_i, M_j] = 2M_k, [M_j, M_k] = 2M_i, [M_k, M_i] = 2M_j — the \mathfrak{su}(2) commutation relations with structure constant +2.

Geometrically this is the quaternionic twist: flowing along M_i preserves its own complex structure but rotates the two complementary structures into one another, and the bracket above measures exactly that torsion.
